about: Each system of the results: what it is, the version and settings the release run used, what it is not given and why, its paper and its link. release/results/rel/panels.py copies it into the results page's categories.json, and each system's page shows it. The facts come from docs/baselines.md and scripts/bench.py; each citation from the system's own repository, site or artifact.

tddlog.about: Exact inference for probabilistic logic programs by Tp-compilation into tree decision diagrams, built bottom-up.
tddlog.settings: Its default strategy (auto) on every instance. Every answer is checked against a reference: ProbLog's, an exact solver written for the suite, the clique tree, Ace or Merlin.

problog.about: The reference implementation of ProbLog: it grounds the program and compiles it into a d-DNNF or an SDD.
problog.settings: Three compilers: d-DNNF (-k ddnnf), SDD (-k sdd) and forward SDD (-k fsdd); each instance counts the fastest. On the Dice paper's loops it is scored on the loops unrolled step by step, the form on which it answers more of them.

cite.authors: Daan Fierens, Guy Van den Broeck, Joris Renkens, Dimitar Shterionov, Bernd Gutmann, Ingo Thon, Gerda Janssens and Luc De Raedt
cite.title: Inference and learning in probabilistic logic programs using weighted Boolean formulas
cite.venue: Theory and Practice of Logic Programming

pita.about: Probabilistic Inference with Tabling and Answer subsumption, part of cplint: it tables the program with answer subsumption and builds BDDs with CUDD.
pita.settings: The ProbLog program in cplint's syntax (problog2pita.py). On the Dice paper's loops it is scored on the recursion, the form on which it answers more of them.

cite.authors: Fabrizio Riguzzi and Terrance Swift
cite.title: The PITA system: Tabling and answer subsumption for reasoning under uncertainty
cite.venue: Theory and Practice of Logic Programming

aspmc.about: Algebraic answer set counting: it reads ProbLog, breaks cycles by Tp-unfolding and counts a Clark completion guided by a tree decomposition.
aspmc.settings: The ProbLog program (-m problog), counted by the knowledge compiler sharpSAT-TD. On the Dice paper's loops it is scored on the loops unrolled step by step, the form on which it answers more of them.

cite.authors: Thomas Eiter, Markus Hecher and Rafael Kiesel
cite.title: Treewidth-aware cycle breaking for algebraic answer set counting

ace.about: Compiles a Bayesian network into an arithmetic circuit, by tabular variable elimination or by encoding it as CNF and compiling with c2d.
ace.settings: Three forms: its default route, c2d forced (-forceC2d), and the circuit evaluated in log space (-Xlog) against underflow; each instance counts the fastest. Its Java heap is half of the lane's memory.

cite.authors: Mark Chavira and Adnan Darwiche
cite.title: On probabilistic inference by weighted model counting

merlin.about: A C++ solver for exact and approximate inference on graphical models in the UAI format.
merlin.settings: Bucket-tree elimination (-a bte) along a min-fill order, on the UAI file and its evidence.

agrum.about: A toolbox for probabilistic graphical models (aGrUM in C++, pyAgrum in Python); here its exact inference.
agrum.settings: LazyPropagation on a Bayesian network and ShaferShenoyMRFInference on a Markov network, the evidence sliced out of the tables (bn_uai_run.py).

cite.authors: Gaspard Ducamp, Christophe Gonzales and Pierre-Henri Wuillemin
cite.title: aGrUM/pyAgrum: a toolbox to build models and algorithms for probabilistic graphical models in Python

pgmpy.about: A Python library for Bayesian networks and other graphical models; here its variable elimination.
pgmpy.settings: VariableElimination, a marginal asked one variable at a time (bn_uai_run.py).

cite.authors: Ankur Ankan and Johannes Textor
cite.title: pgmpy: A Python toolkit for Bayesian networks

libdai.about: A C++ library for inference in graphical models; here its exact junction tree.
libdai.settings: JTree with HUGIN updates and a min-fill order (libdai_uai.cpp).

cite.authors: Joris M. Mooij
cite.title: libDAI: A free and open source C++ library for discrete approximate inference in graphical models

tensorinference.about: Exact inference on graphical models by tensor network contraction, in Julia.
tensorinference.settings: Two contraction orders, TreeSA (the package's default) and greedy; each instance counts the faster (tensorinference_uai.jl).

cite.authors: Martin Roa-Villescas and Jin-Guo Liu
cite.title: TensorInference: A Julia package for tensor-based probabilistic inference

dice.about: A discrete probabilistic programming language whose programs compile into BDDs in the order of the program text.
dice.version: Dice 1.0, the binary of the sholtzen/dice image
dice.settings: The Dice program as written, with an unlimited stack.

cite.authors: Steven Holtzen, Guy Van den Broeck and Todd Millstein
cite.title: Scaling exact inference for discrete probabilistic programs

alea.about: The Julia successor of Dice: distributions and integers are Julia values, bit-blasted and compiled into BDDs with CUDD.
alea.version: Alea.jl at revision cf5e5b8 on Julia 1.11.9 with CUDD 3.0.0, one thread
alea.settings: Dice programs through dice2alea.py. Its time is the one it reports for building the model and computing its answers a second time in the same process, without Julia's compilation, as its papers time it; the process's wall time is on the suites' pages.

cite.authors: Poorva Garg, Steven Holtzen, Guy Van den Broeck and Todd Millstein
cite.title: Bit blasting probabilistic programs

roulette.about: A discrete probabilistic language embedded in Racket, compiled into BDDs through Rosette's symbolic evaluation.
roulette.version: Roulette of its PLDI 2025 artifact (revision 54d6185) on Racket 8.16
roulette.settings: Dice programs through dice2roulette.py. Three forms, the artifact's (rsdd), without its complement (nocomplement, on the translated programs) and, on a network that observes nothing, the network built by the artifact's bayes.rkt from a BIF file (bayes); each instance counts the fastest. Its time is the one the artifact's own time reports, without Racket's start-up.

cite.authors: Cameron Moy, Jack Czenszak, John M. Li, Brianna Marshall and Steven Holtzen
cite.title: Roulette: A language for expressive, exact, and efficient discrete probabilistic programming

nodice.about: Exact inference for discrete probabilistic programs with nondeterminism and conditioning, in Dice's syntax.
nodice.settings: The Dice program as written; it prints six digits.

cite.authors: Tobias Gürtler and Benjamin Lucien Kaminski
cite.title: noDice: Inference for discrete probabilistic programs with nondeterminism and conditioning

psi.about: Exact symbolic inference for probabilistic programs.
psi.settings: Dice programs through dice2psi.py. Psi answers one expression, so a program runs once for each component of its value and the times add up.

cite.authors: Timon Gehr, Sasa Misailovic and Martin Vechev
cite.title: PSI: Exact symbolic inference for probabilistic programs

genfer.about: Exact Bayesian inference on discrete models through probability generating functions.
genfer.settings: Dice programs through dice2genfer.py; its own programs as its repository ships them, with --rational where their probabilities are rational.

cite.authors: Fabian Zaiser, Andrzej S. Murawski and Luke Ong
cite.title: Exact Bayesian inference on discrete models via probability generating functions: A probabilistic programming approach

sppl.about: Probabilistic programming with exact symbolic inference over sum-product expressions.
sppl.settings: Dice programs through dice2sppl.py; its own Markov switching model as its notebook runs it.

cite.authors: Feras A. Saad, Martin C. Rinard and Vikash K. Mansinghka
cite.title: SPPL: Probabilistic programming with fast exact symbolic inference

geni.about: Compiles discrete probabilistic programs into generating functions.
geni.settings: Dice programs through dice2geni.py, run as gennifer -l -i FILE; it prints seven decimals.

cite.authors: Jianlin Li and Yizhou Zhang
cite.title: Compiling with generating functions

pluck.about: Lazy knowledge compilation of discrete probabilistic programs into BDDs.
pluck.version: Pluck of its PLDI 2025 artifact (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.15051140) on Julia 1.11.9, with rsdd
pluck.settings: Dice programs through dice2pluck.py, run through bdd_forward as the artifact's harness runs them.
pluck.notgiven: The UAI 2022 sets of partition functions, for lack of time in this release.

cite.authors: Maddy Bowers, Alexander K. Lew, Joshua B. Tenenbaum, Armando Solar-Lezama and Vikash K. Mansinghka
cite.title: Stochastic lazy knowledge compilation for inference in discrete probabilistic programs

storm.about: A probabilistic model checker; here it computes the probability of a program's result on the program's Markov chain.
storm.version: Storm 1.14 through stormpy, one Sylvan thread
storm.settings: Three engines: the explicit model in doubles (sparse) and in rationals (exact), and decision diagrams (dd); each instance counts the fastest. It reads Rubicon's PRISM models of the weather factory, and the Markov chain that dice2prism.py writes of every other Dice program.
storm.notgiven: The UAI 2022 sets of partition functions, for lack of time in this release.

cite.authors: Christian Hensel, Sebastian Junges, Joost-Pieter Katoen, Tim Quatmann and Matthias Volk
cite.title: The probabilistic model checker Storm
cite.venue: International Journal on Software Tools for Technology Transfer

prism.about: A probabilistic model checker; here on the same Markov chains as Storm.
prism.settings: Two engines, the explicit one (sparse) and its default hybrid one; each instance counts the faster.
prism.notgiven: The UAI 2022 sets of partition functions, for lack of time in this release.

cite.authors: Marta Kwiatkowska, Gethin Norman and David Parker
cite.title: PRISM 4.0: Verification of probabilistic real-time systems

provsql.about: A PostgreSQL extension that tracks the provenance of query results and computes their probability.
provsql.settings: The database and the query as SQL over tuple-independent tables (tpch2provsql.py); probability_evaluate picks its method by cost.
provsql.notgiven: Every program its translation cannot express: a recursive rule, a probabilistic rule or an annotated disjunction (which would need a fresh tuple for each grounding), the networks of the network suites, and the Dice and Alea.jl programs.

cite.authors: Aryak Sen, Silviu Maniu and Pierre Senellart
cite.title: ProvSQL: A general system for keeping track of the provenance and probability of data

psouffle.about: An exact probabilistic Datalog compiler and runtime built on Soufflé: the compiled program records each rule application in a derivation graph and compiles the graph's components into BDDs.
psouffle.settings: The ProbLog program written as a Soufflé program (problog2souffle.py) and compiled untimed (souffle --full-only), as its paper times inference; the run is timed, in its default full inference on one thread (--jobs=1); its graph rewrites (--rewrite) lose derivations at this commit and are not used.
psouffle.notgiven: The networks and the probabilistic functional programs, for lack of time in this release; the programs its language cannot express (lists, function symbols, disjunctive bodies, division, negation through recursion).

cite.authors: Xuyang Li, Jiahao Xia, Ahmed Adnan and Jingbo Wang
cite.title: PSoufflé: Scaling Exact Probabilistic Logic Inference for Program Analysis

scallop.about: A Datalog language for neurosymbolic programming whose provenance semirings tag each tuple: for probabilities its top-k proofs keep the k most probable proofs of each tuple and count the weighted models of their disjunction with an SDD.
scallop.settings: The ground program tddlog --ground prints, as Scallop relations and rules (ground2scallop.py), under its top-k proofs (-p topkproofs) at the largest k its command line takes, 2^64 - 1, so that no proof is dropped and the answer is exact (allproofs); its time includes the grounding. Scallop does not condition: with evidence the harness divides the probability of the query and the evidence by that of the evidence, and for a partition function it is asked the probability of the evidence as a query, as ProbLog is.

cite.authors: Ziyang Li, Jiani Huang and Mayur Naik
cite.title: Scallop: A Language for Neurosymbolic Programming
